issues.title: Point-in-time triple trajectory truncates before the as_of filter
issues.why_it_matters: temporal_history is the NFR-4 point-in-time read. When a (subject, predicate) has more versions than the hard limit, the SQL LIMIT is applied to the oldest rows first and as_of is filtered afterward, so a query 'as of date X' can omit the version that was current at X and answer with an older state.
issues.impact: Silent wrong point-in-time answer whenever version count > limit (default 20, max 200). Untested because T100150-08 uses only 2 versions and the limit test uses no as_of.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_history_read.rs:282-289 orders `ORDER BY tx_from, id LIMIT ?4` (ascending, oldest first); crates/clio-store/src/postgres_history_read.rs:196-207 same; crates/clio-history/src/temporal.rs:248-263 filters `valid_from <= as_of` / `tx_from <= as_of` client-side after the fetch.
issues.proposed_fix: Push the as_of predicate into the SQL (add as_of/axis parameters to triple_history, or fetch the newest N at/under as_of via a subquery) so filtering happens before limiting; add a regression test with 3+ versions, limit=2, and as_of beyond the limit that asserts the entry current at as_of is returned.

issues.title: 12 new Rust test/support files lack the AGENTS.md-mandated module header
issues.why_it_matters: AGENTS.md and the developer prompt require the exact header (`# Responsibility`, `## Owns`, `## Does not own`, `## Boundary`) on every new/modified Rust source file. Existing test files in this repo follow it, so the new files are inconsistent and violate a hard rule.
issues.impact: Process/consistency violation; ownership statements absent for 12 files.
issues.evidence: Missing header in crates/clio-history/src/{domain_tests,failure_tests,lib_tests,postgres_parity_tests,retry_tests,similar_tests,task_tests,temporal_tests,test_support}.rs, crates/clio-store/src/{pg_history_tests,sqlite_history_tests}.rs, crates/clio-types/src/history_tests.rs (each begins with only copyright + a one-line //!). Contrast crates/clio-retrieve/src/assoc_tests.rs:1-8 and crates/clio-store/src/triple_tests.rs:1-6.
issues.proposed_fix: Add the standard Responsibility/Owns/Does-not-own/Boundary header to each of the 12 files.

issues.title: T100150-13 'compose persona unchanged' is not tested as specified
issues.why_it_matters: The phase's required scenario T100150-13 says failures must not enter the persona channel, verified by compose persona remaining unchanged. The test only checks a domain-membership predicate; it never runs compose/persona injection. AC-100150-06 is marked PASS on weaker evidence than the scenario demands.
issues.impact: A regression that routed failure carriers into the always-on persona channel would not be caught by the current tests.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-history/src/domain_tests.rs:100-124; roadmap phase file AC-100150-06 row and T100150-13 row.
issues.proposed_fix: Add a regression test that seeds a failure record and asserts compose_context/persona injection output is byte-identical to the same compose without the failure (or that no failure-derived text appears in the persona pack).

issues.title: T100150-11/T100150-12 are tested at the predicate level, not through hybrid retrieve; no explicit no-full-log assertion
issues.why_it_matters: T100150-11 is specified as 'retrieve domain=failure returns only failure hits' and Task 5 required an explicit assertion that a list-all-messages API does not exist. The tests call `item_in_domains` directly and assert limit caps; they do not exercise the retrieve pipeline or assert API absence.
issues.impact: A break in the retrieve/index wiring for failure carriers would pass the current tests.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-history/src/domain_tests.rs:52-55 uses `clio_retrieve::item_in_domains`; :59-98 only checks resolve_limit and returned row counts.
issues.proposed_fix: Add an integration test that runs the hybrid retriever with domains=[Failure] against a store containing task, failure, and unrelated episodic items and asserts only failure-typed hits; add an explicit negative assertion (e.g. grep-style source assertion or absence of any unbounded-read API) for T100150-12.

issues.title: No cross-bank rejection test for task/failure history
issues.why_it_matters: The phase's Security Acceptance Conditions require 'Cross-bank task history access rejected'. The SQL is bank-scoped, but the required security test is absent.
issues.impact: Isolation is structurally sound but not regression-guarded.
issues.evidence: grep for cross_bank|bank-b|other_bank in crates/clio-history/src and the new clio-store history tests returned no matches; queries are bank-scoped at crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_history_read.rs:146-150 and :213-216.
issues.proposed_fix: Add a test that writes a task/failure in bank A and asserts get_task/get_failure/failures_for_task/task_history against bank B return None/empty.

issues.why_it_matters: The phase's Completion Evidence says 'clio-history/src/* functions 100%', but temporal.rs is 11/12 functions (91.67%). Honest evidence is a hard requirement.
issues.impact: A reviewer trusting the phase file would overstate coverage; still above the 90% gate, so no gate failure.

issues.title: Default thresholds not documented in config as Task 3 required
issues.why_it_matters: Phase Task 3 Required Changes #3 says 'Document default thresholds in config'. Defaults live in clio-types::HistoryPolicy with no clio-config surface; the developer disclosed this as a known limitation.
issues.impact: Deployments cannot tune the similarity threshold/lesson cap through the config tools; behavior is still documented in code.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-history/src/similar.rs:23-28 and crates/clio-types/src/history.rs:29-60; phase Known limitations bullet 3.
issues.proposed_fix: Either add a config profile/knob for lesson_max_tokens and similarity_threshold or record an explicit approved exception to the Task 3 requirement.

issues.title: failure_record validates attempt_n only after running the admission gate
issues.why_it_matters: attempt_n < 1 is rejected by the store (draft.validate) only after gated_create has decided and emitted an admit_accept event, so telemetry records an accepted write for a record that is never stored.
issues.impact: Minor telemetry/audit inconsistency; no data loss.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-history/src/failure.rs:94-135 has no attempt_n check before gated_create; crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_history_write.rs:204 calls draft.validate() inside the write closure; crates/clio-history/src/failure_tests.rs:161 expects OutOfRange from the store.
issues.proposed_fix: Validate attempt_n >= 1 (and other draft invariants) before constructing the gate request.

issues.title: what_failed is uncapped and returned on every failure read
issues.why_it_matters: Only `lesson` is length-capped; `what_failed` accepts arbitrary free text, is encrypted at rest, and is returned by get_failure/failures_for_task. The phase's stated abuse control is a lesson cap, but an unbounded what_failed is still a token/abuse vector on the read path.
issues.impact: A caller can store very large what_failed payloads; bounded read limits cap row count, not row size.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-history/src/failure.rs:97 checks only non-empty; cap applied only to lesson at :99 via crates/clio-types/src/history.rs:126; what_failed read at crates/clio-store/src/sqlite_history_read.rs:129.
issues.proposed_fix: Apply a documented cap to what_failed (or document explicitly why only lesson is bounded), and test the over-cap path.

strengths: Atomic write path mirrors the existing commit_triple_add pattern: gated carrier item + structured row + audit event + index enqueue in one transaction, with DEK-sealed content.
Clean separation: clio-types shapes/policy, clio-store HistoryStore contract with per-backend SQL files, clio-history tool/façade layer — each new file stays well under 450 lines.
Exact-first then similar-second FR-9 path with 6 retitle fixtures and a passing opt-in Postgres parity test.
All reads resolve a hard limit; there is genuinely no full-log API.
Lesson over-cap is rejected before any gate/write, and the FailureRecord shape matches §7.3 (epistemic_kind=belief) including a DB CHECK constraint.
regrets: Should have constructed a live >limit + as_of triple fixture to turn the point-in-time finding from code-reading into a reproduced failure; the logic is unambiguous but a runtime demonstration would be stronger.
Could not run `make check` literally (it writes formatting via `cargo fmt --all`); ran the three components individually to avoid modifying the working tree.
